title: しばらく — for a while
summary: An adverb for a period of time whose length is not exact. It can mean a short while (“please wait a moment”) or a fairly long time (“I haven't seen you for a while”). The context shows how long.

patterns.gloss: for a while (しばらく待つ)

patterns.form: しばらくすると／しばらくして
patterns.gloss: after a little while (しばらくすると店員が来る)

body.p: As in こちらでしばらくお待ちください, it expresses a brief period in requests and announcements. It feels a little longer than 少々 and is handy when the wait is not specific. しばらくすると〜 means “after a little while,” when something happens later.

With a negative or past form, as in しばらく会っていない or しばらくぶり, it can mean quite a long period, from weeks to years. It is nearly the same as 久しぶり and works as a greeting (しばらくでした). The length depends on the speaker's sense.

examples.ja: こちらでしばらくお待（ま）ちください。
examples.tr: Please wait here for a while.

examples.ja: 引（ひ）っ越（こ）してから、しばらく友（とも）だちに会（あ）っていない。
examples.romaji: Hikkoshite kara, shibaraku tomodachi ni atte inai.
examples.tr: Since I moved, I haven't seen my friends for a while.

examples.ja: 少々（しょうしょう）お待（ま）ちください。しばらくすると店員（てんいん）が参（まい）ります。
examples.romaji: Shōshō omachi kudasai. Shibaraku suru to ten'in ga mairimasu.
examples.tr: Please wait a moment. In a little while a clerk will come.
examples.note: しばらくすると = after a little while.

pitfalls: Its length is vague; when you need an exact time (such as thirty minutes), give the number.
It also appears as しばらくの間. It is not used like an adjective, as in “しばらくな.”
